What is the atomic number of Unbihexium?
Unbihexium, also known as element 126 or eka-plutonium, is a hypothetical chemical element; it has atomic number 126 and placeholder symbol Ubh.
In what year was Steve Jobs born?
Steve Jobs: Steven Paul Jobs (February 24, 1955 – October 5, 2011) was an American businessman, inventor, and investor.
In what year was Silver discovered?
Silver is a chemical element; it has symbol Ag (from Latin argentum 'silver') and atomic number 47.
In what year was Manganese discovered?
Manganese is a chemical element; it has the symbol Mn and atomic number 25.

In which country is Junkers Ju 52?
Junkers Ju 52: Germany. Development of the Ju 52 commenced in the late 1920s, headed by German aeronautical engineer Ernst Zindel.

Sodium: Humphry Davy. Sodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Na (from Neo-Latin natrium) and atomic number 11.
This long-term skin condition occurs when dead skin cells and oil clog hair follicles, producing blackheads, whiteheads, and pimples mainly on the face, chest, and back — what is it?
Acne is a long-term skin condition that occurs when dead skin cells and sebum clog hair follicles.
This large, muscular mastiff-type dog breed descends from ancestors brought to the British North American colonies, where they worked on small farms and ranches — what's the breed?
American Bulldog is a large, muscular breed of mastiff-type dog.
With 1,248 built, this turboprop's design was adapted from an earlier Soviet transport aircraft and became NATO's 'Cub' — which four-engine workhorse?
Antonov An-12 (NATO reporting name: Cub) is a four-engined turboprop transport aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Once native to the highland lakes of Xochimilco and Chalco, this neotenic mole salamander keeps its external gills and stays aquatic for life — what is it?
Axolotl (from Classical; Ambystoma mexicanum) is a species of mole salamander.

The bassist of a legendary British rock band from 1962 to 1993, performing on its first 19 studio albums, this musician was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1989 as part of that group — who is he?
Bill Wyman (n Perks; born 24 October 1936) is an English musician who was the bassist of the rock band the Rolling Stones from 1962 to 1993.
This rhythmic bodily process draws oxygen-rich air into the lungs and expels carbon dioxide, powering the cellular chemistry that turns food into energy — what process is it?
Breathing (respiring or ventilating) is the rhythmic process of inhaling air into the lungs providing oxygen, and exhaling the air removing carbon dioxide, in the gas exchange process.
Prized in India for hashish and cultivated from China to West Africa, this Hindu Kush-native plant produces cannabinoid levels well above ordinary hemp — which species?
Cannabis indica is an annual plant species in the family Cannabaceae indigenous to the Hindu Kush mountains of Southern Asia.
Built under license from the Soviet MiG-21, this Chinese fighter jet carries the NATO reporting name Fishcan and specializes in short-range air combat — what aircraft is it?
Chengdu J-7 (pinyin: Jin-7; third generation export version J-7; NATO reporting name: Fishcan) is a Chinese fighter aircraft.
The smallest member of the cockatoo family, this Australian parrot is recognized for its expressive crest and long tail feathers, and is a hugely popular pet bird. What bird is it?

Cockatiel (Nymphicus hollandicus), also known as the weero/weiro or quarrion, is a species of small- to medium-sized parrot belonging to the cockatoo family (Cacatuidae), of which it is the smallest member.

This family of fifteen tall, long-necked bird species mostly wears muted gray-and-white plumage with a patch of bare red skin on the face — except for one crowned genus that stands out — what bird is it?
Crane (bird) are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes.
This colourless, highly volatile, sweet-smelling organic compound with formula (CH3CH2)2O was once used as a general anesthetic and remains a common laboratory solvent — what is it?
This American physicist was the first to make a transuranium element, neptunium, sharing the 1951 Nobel Prize in Chemistry with Glenn Seaborg. Who was he?
Edwin McMillan (September 18, 1907 - September 7, 1991) was an American physicist credited with being the first to produce a transuranium element, neptunium.

This branch of anthropology systematically studies individual cultures from the point of view of the people within them, relying heavily on researchers directly participating in the settings they study — what is this method called?
Ethnography is a branch of anthropology and the systematic study of individual cultures. It explores cultural phenomena from the point of view of the subject of the study.
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive it combines with nearly every other element except the light noble gases. What element is it (symbol F)?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has the symbol F and atomic number 9.
With the symbol Ge and atomic number 32, this lustrous, brittle metalloid was predicted to exist by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869, decades before it was actually discovered — name this element?
Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
This North Atlantic member of the true cod family is a fisheries staple in northern Europe, often smoked into varieties like Finnan haddie and the Arbroath smokie — what is it?
Haddock (Melanogrammus aeglefinus) is a saltwater ray-finned fish from the family Gadidae, the true cods.

This extinct human species from the Middle Pleistocene may represent the last common ancestor of modern humans, Neanderthals, and Denisovans — or a completely separate lineage altogether — what species is it?
Homo heidelbergensis is a species of archaic human from the Middle Pleistocene of Europe and Africa, as well as potentially Asia depending on the taxonomic convention used.
This Russian-American aviation pioneer, a trailblazer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft, won the top prize at the 1912 Moscow Aviation Exhibition for one of his early designs — who is he?
Igor Sikorsky (25 May 1889 - 26 October 1972) was a Russian-American aviation pioneer in both helicopters and fixed-wing aircraft.

Designed under the philosophy 'write once, run anywhere,' this high-level, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language compiles to bytecode executed by a dedicated virtual machine — name the language?
Java (programming language) is a high-level, general-purpose, memory-safe, object-oriented programming language.
This pain-relieving, fever-reducing drug belongs to the propionic acid class of anti-inflammatories and hit the market in 1980, thirteen years after being patented — what is it?
Ketoprofen is one of the propionic acid class of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID) with analgesic and antipyretic effects.
This American computer scientist won the 2013 Turing Award for taming the chaos of distributed systems — and, on the side, created the document-preparation system LaTeX — who is he?
Leslie Lamport (born February 7, 1941) is an American computer scientist and mathematician.
This paired organ, located near the backbone on either side of the heart in most mammals, extracts oxygen from the air and releases carbon dioxide back into it — name the organ?
Lung are the primary organs of the respiratory system in many animals, including humans.
Working on the geometry of Riemann surfaces, this Tehran-born Stanford professor became in 2014 the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal — who was she?
Maryam Mirzakhani (12 May 1977 - 14 July 2017) was an Iranian mathematician and a professor of mathematics at Stanford University.
Carrying NATO's 'Hind' codename and its crews' affectionate 'flying tank,' this Soviet machine is both an attack craft and a low-capacity troop carrier. What is it?
Mil Mi-24 (NATO reporting name: Hind) is a large helicopter gunship, attack helicopter and low-capacity troop transport with room for eight passengers.

In this group of bone-marrow cancers, blood cells fail to mature properly and never develop into healthy cells, early on there are often no symptoms, though it can progress into acute leukemia. Name the condition?
Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) is one of a group of cancers in which blood cells in the bone marrow do not mature, and as a result, do not develop into healthy blood cells.
This American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth bomber, solely operated by the US Air Force, is designed as a flying wing to penetrate sophisticated air defenses. What is this aircraft?
Northrop B-2 Spirit is an American nuclear-capable subsonic stealth strategic bomber, often referred to as a "stealth bomber", solely operated by the United States Air Force.
It surges during childbirth and sexual activity, drives maternal bonding and milk production, and is released by the posterior pituitary — which hormone is this?
Oxytocin is a peptide hormone and neuropeptide normally produced in the hypothalamus and released by the posterior pituitary.
This inflammation of the lining of the abdominal cavity can be caused by a ruptured appendix, a perforated ulcer, or pancreatitis, and may lead to shock if untreated. What condition is it?
Peritonitis is inflammation of the localized or generalized peritoneum, the lining of the inner wall of the abdomen and covering of the abdominal organs.
Caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis and often spread by flea bites, this disease comes in pneumonic, bubonic, and septicemic forms — what is it?
Plague (disease) is an infectious disease caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis. There are three forms of plague, each affecting a different part of the body and causing associated symptoms.
Used to treat high blood pressure, irregular heart rhythms, performance anxiety and migraine prevention, this beta blocker medication reaches the bloodstream within 30 minutes of dosing — which drug?
Propranolol is a medication of the beta blocker class. It can be taken orally, rectally, or by intravenous injection.

One of 36 species-rich pit vipers found mainly in the Americas, this snake shakes a noisy tail segment to warn off predators and is responsible for most snakebite injuries in North America — which snake?
Rattlesnake are venomous snakes that form the genera Crotalus and Sistrurus of the subfamily Crotalinae (the pit vipers).

Known by folk names like knotberry and lowbush salmonberry, this amber fruit structurally similar to a blackberry thrives in Arctic tundra and boreal forest but isn't farmed commercially — which species?
Rubus chamaemorus (also known as cloudberry) is a species of flowering plant in the rose family, Rosaceae.
This interdisciplinary field studies signs and sign systems, breaking down into branches examining the formal relations between signs, their meanings, and their users — what's the field called?
Semiotics is the study of signs. It is an interdisciplinary field that examines what signs are, how they form sign systems, and how individuals use them to communicate meaning.
This plant family includes both deadly poisonous species and kitchen staples like tomatoes, potatoes, and peppers, all linked by unusually high alkaloid content — what family is it?
Solanaceae is a family of flowering plants in the order Solanales.
In the equation 5 − 2 = 3, this is the operation being performed — which one is it?
Subtraction (which is signified by the minus sign) is one of the four arithmetic operations along with addition, multiplication and division.

This mass of gray matter forming part of the forebrain relays sensory and motor signals to the cerebral cortex through radiating nerve fibers, and helps regulate consciousness, sleep, and alertness — what's the structure?
Thalamus (pl.: thalami; from Greek, "chamber") is a large mass of gray matter on the lateral wall of the third ventricle forming the dorsal part of the diencephalon (a division of the forebrain).
Taken by mouth, injection, or inhalation, this steroid helps prevent asthma and COPD flare-ups from worsening — which medication?
Triamcinolone is a glucocorticoid used to treat certain skin diseases, allergies, and rheumatic disorders among others.
Its Latin name means 'maiden,' and it's the largest zodiac grouping in the sky, home to the bright star Spica between Leo and Libra — which one?
Virgo (constellation) is one of the constellations of the zodiac. The ecliptic intersects the celestial equator within this constellation and Pisces.

A rapid rise-and-fall of voltage across a cell membrane, this "spike" depolarizes neighboring spots and is how neurons and muscle cells fire — what is this electrical event called?
Action potential: Neuron communication by electric impulses.
Beginning about six hours after someone dependent on drinking stops, this set of symptoms can include shaking, sweating, seizures, and life-threatening delirium -- what is it called?
Over 500 of these organic compounds exist in nature, yet only 22 appear in the genetic code, joining together to build proteins — what are they?
Amino acid: Organic compounds containing amine and carboxylic groups.
Awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2008 for his AIDS-relief work on PEPFAR, this immunologist directed the U.S. allergy and infectious-disease institute from 1984 to 2022. Who is he?
Known as common wormwood, this bitter herb native to North Africa and temperate Eurasia lends its name and flavor to a notorious green spirit — which plant?
Artemisia absinthium: Species of plant. It is grown as an ornamental plant and is used as an ingredient in the spirit absinthe and some other alcoholic beverages.
Blooming for weeks each spring and thriving in the shade under trees, these flowering shrubs belong to the genus Rhododendron — what are they called?
Azalea: Subgroup of rhododendron flowering shrubs.
A likely hybrid of lemon and a bitter citrus relative, this fragrant fruit flavors tea, snus, and perfume, though it can heighten skin's sensitivity to sunlight — which fruit?
Originally launched as the McDonnell Douglas MD-95, this narrow-body airliner seats up to 134 passengers with twin engines mounted at the tail — which jet?
Ranging from roughly seawater-strength up to a fully saturated 26%, which salty solution is used for pickling food, de-icing roads, and turns up as a wastewater byproduct of desalination?
Brine: Concentrated solution of salt in water.
Named for the Latin word for the first day of the month, this daisy-family genus is commonly called marigold and is prized in herbal and cosmetic products — which plant?
Calendula: Genus of flowering plants in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Its Greek-derived genus name Xylocopa literally means 'wood-cutter,' fitting for an insect that burrows nesting tunnels into dead wood or bamboo — which insect is it?
Carpenter bee: Common name for a genus of bees.
Also known as silver beet or perpetual spinach, this leafy green shares its species with beetroot — which vegetable?
Chard: Green leafy vegetable. Chard (Beta vulgaris subsp. vulgaris, Cicla Group and Flavescens Group) is a green leafy vegetable.
Sold under the brand name Celexa, this SSRI antidepressant treats major depressive disorder, OCD, panic disorder, and social anxiety — what is it?
Citalopram: SSRI antidepressant. Citalopram, sold under the brand name Celexa among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
This icy wanderer of the solar system grows a gassy halo and sometimes a tail stretching more than an astronomical unit as it nears the sun — what is it?
Comet: Natural object in space that releases gas.
Spread mainly through the fecal-oral route, these single-stranded RNA enteroviruses share traits with poliovirus and rank among the leading causes of aseptic meningitis — which pathogens?
Coxsackievirus: Virus that causes digestive upset and sometimes heart damage.
This Harvard-trained legal scholar who wrote on criminal punishment and retribution joined Florida State's faculty in 2005, and was later murdered in a plot tied to his ex-wife's family — who is he?
Dan Markel: American law professor and murder victim (1972–2014)
This colorless, highly flammable liquid with a sweet smell was once widely used as a general anesthetic before modern alternatives — what compound?
After co-founding a social media giant, this entrepreneur left in 2008 to launch the workplace software company Asana — who is he?
Nicknamed the ALX, this Brazilian turboprop light-attack aircraft is assembled in Jacksonville, Florida with an American defense partner for low-threat counter-insurgency missions — which aircraft?
Embraer EMB 314 Super Tucano: Light ground attack and training aircraft.
Odorless, colorless, and dangerously sweet-tasting, this viscous compound goes into polyester fibers and antifreeze — and has even been spotted in outer space. What is it?
Born in 1963, this woman is the daughter of the last Shah of Iran by his third wife — who is she?
Sold under the brand name Prozac, this SSRI treats depression, OCD and panic disorder, and is also prescribed off-label for premature ejaculation — what is it?
Fluoxetine: SSRI antidepressant. It is also approved for treatment of major depressive disorder in adolescents and children 8 years of age and over.
With a melting point of just under 30 degrees Celsius, this metal will turn to liquid in the palm of your hand — which element?
Gallium: Chemical element with atomic number 31 (Ga)
Found in birds, crocodilians, and earthworms alike, this thick-muscled digestive organ grinds food with the help of swallowed grit — what's it called?
Gizzard: Digestive organ of some animals.

This algebraic structure — a set paired with an operation that's associative, has an identity element, and gives every member an inverse — is exemplified by the integers under addition. What is it called?

Group (mathematics): Set with associative invertible operation. The concept of a group was elaborated for handling, in a unified way, many mathematical structures such as numbers, geometric shapes and polynomial roots.
About the size of a closed fist and enclosed in a protective sac called the pericardium, this four-chambered organ sits in the chest between the lungs and pumps blood through the body — which organ?
Heart: Organ found in humans and other animals.
This genus of over 570 flowering plants — the only living genus in its family — includes the evergreen shrub famous for Christmas decorations and cards. What genus is it?
Holly: Genus of flowering plants. Ilex or holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.

This neurological disorder involves excessive sleepiness or time spent sleeping, sometimes linked to seasonal affective disorder, and appears under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5 — what is it called?

Hypersomnia: Neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness. It can have many possible causes (such as seasonal affective disorder) and can cause distress and problems with functioning.
More than half of all animal species belong to this one chitinous-shelled group, each member sporting three body parts and three pairs of jointed legs — who are they?
Known as sampaguita in the Philippines, where it's the national flower, this fragrant vine or shrub also lends its blossoms to a beloved variety of tea — which species?
Jasminum sambac: Species of jasmine. Jasminum sambac (Arabian jasmine or Sambac jasmine or Mogra) is a species of jasmine native to Bhutan and India.
Also nicknamed the reed or swamp feline, this solitary wild predator ranges from the Caucasus to Southeast Asia and marks territory by urine spraying — which species?
Biosynthesized in the body from the amino acid tyrosine, this compound is the direct precursor to dopamine, norepinephrine, and epinephrine — what is it?
L-DOPA: Chemical compound. As is true for many molecules, the human body produces only one of these isomers (the l-DOPA form).

Elon Musk's praise for his MIT driver-attention study on Tesla's autopilot brought this computer scientist to prominence in 2019, ahead of a career hosting long-form interviews with notable figures — who is he?
Lex Fridman: American scientist and podcast host (born 1983)
Sold under the brand name Cozaar, this angiotensin receptor blocker treats high blood pressure while also protecting the kidneys in diabetic patients — what drug is it?
Losartan: Blood pressure medication. Losartan, sold under the brand name Cozaar among others, is a medication used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension).
This genus of some 32 to 57 deciduous tree and shrub species in the rose family includes the domesticated orchard fruit tree along with crab and wild varieties — what genus is it?
Malus: Flowering genus, rose family Rosaceae.

The largest trijet ever built, this American wide-body airliner first flew in January 1990 and entered service with Finnair that December, a stretched, winglet-equipped update of an earlier trijet — what is it?
McDonnell Douglas MD-11: Wide body airliners developed from the DC-10.
Despite little formal schooling, this self-taught English scientist uncovered the principles behind electromagnetic induction and established the concept of the electromagnetic field — who is he?
Michael Faraday: English chemist and physicist (1791–1867)
Originally a dry-season staple for ǃKung hunter-gatherers, this tropical vine in the Cucurbitaceae family produces an intensely bitter edible fruit widely used across Asian cuisine — what is it?
Momordica charantia: Species of plant in the gourd family.

It strikes when blood flow to the heart muscle stops, killing tissue — classically a crushing chest pain that radiates to the left arm or jaw, though women more often feel only neck pain or fatigue. What is this medical emergency?
Myocardial infarction: Interruption of cardiac blood supply.
An oily alkaloid from nightshade plants like tobacco, it doubles as a potent insect neurotoxin and once served as an insecticide, inspiring the neonicotinoid pesticides — what is it?
Nicotine: Chemical stimulant produced by some plants.
This physics principle states that current through a conductor is directly proportional to the voltage across it, expressed as V equals I times R — what's it called?
Ohm's law: Law of electrical current and voltage. Ohm's law states that the electric current through a conductor between two points is directly proportional to the voltage across the two points.
A reactive nonmetal of the chalcogen group, it's the most abundant element in Earth's crust — locked into water, silicates, and rust — and the third-most abundant in the universe. What is it?
Oxygen: Chemical element with atomic number 8 (O)
This hickory species native to the Mississippi River region produces a nut used in praline candy and a famous holiday pie, and is the official state tree of Texas — what is it?
Pecan: Species of nut tree native to the southern USA and northern Mexico.
This branch of linguistics studies how speech sounds are articulated, transmitted as sound waves, and perceived, split into three sub-disciplines — what field is it?
Phonetics: Study of how humans produce and perceive sounds.
Sometimes called a 'collapsed lung,' this condition involves air trapped in the space between the lung and chest wall, causing sudden sharp one-sided chest pain — what is it?
Pneumothorax: Abnormal collection of air in the pleural space.
Manufactured in a soybean-oil emulsion that gives it a milky white look, this IV anesthetic — sold as Diprivan — induces unconsciousness fast and lets patients wake quickly; what is it?
Propofol: Intravenous medication used in anesthesia.
Guided by empiricist and positivist philosophy, which academic methodology turns data collection into numbers to test theories across the natural, applied, formal, and social sciences?
Quantitative research: All procedures for the numerical representation of empirical facts.
Native to South and Southeast Asia, this non-venomous constrictor is the world's longest snake and has been spotted swimming far out at sea — what species is it?
Reticulated python: Species of snake. It is the world's longest snake, and the third heaviest after the green anaconda and Burmese python.

Sold under the brand name Crestor, this medication lowers cholesterol by inhibiting an enzyme in the liver called HMG-CoA reductase, and was the twelfth most commonly prescribed drug in the US in 2023. What is it?
Rosuvastatin: Statin medication. It is recommended to be used with dietary changes, exercise, and weight loss.
Also called a green onion, this mild Allium vegetable has a slender green stem but never develops a bulb like its garlic and leek relatives — what is it?
Scallion: Edible vegetable of various species in the genus Allium.
Nicknamed the 'Human Computer' for her lightning mental arithmetic, this Indian writer also authored one of the earliest studies of homosexuality in India, back in 1977 — who is she?
Shakuntala Devi: Indian writer and mental calculator (1929–2013)

Historically mined in vast deposits and nicknamed 'Chile saltpeter,' this white, water-soluble alkali metal compound is used in fertilizers, fireworks, meat preservation, and solid rocket fuel. What is it?
Sodium nitrate: Chemical compound. The mineral form is also known as nitratine, nitratite or soda niter.
Famous for kite-shaped plates along its back and spikes on its tail, this Late Jurassic herbivore may have been preyed on by Allosaurus — which dinosaur?
Stegosaurus: Genus of Late Jurassic armored dinosaur.
Nicknamed 'knitbone' and 'boneset' for its traditional use in healing wounds, this perennial herb carries a liver-toxicity warning against internal use — which plant?
Symphytum officinale: Species of flowering plant in the borage family Boraginaceae.
The primary male sex hormone, this androgen builds muscle and bone, spurs body hair, and is even linked to mood, courtship display and dominance in both sexes — what is it?
Testosterone: Primary male sex hormone. It is associated with increased aggression, sex drive, dominance, courtship display, and a wide range of behavioral characteristics.

First identified in 1846 and nicknamed 'Peter Elam's disease' in parts of South Asia, this skin condition causing patchy discoloration is caused by an overgrowth of Malassezia yeast — what is it called?
Tinea versicolor: Skin disease. Tinea versicolor (also pityriasis versicolor) is a condition characterized by a skin eruption on the trunk and proximal extremities.
One of only a few fish able to keep its body warmer than the surrounding water, this fast-swimming ocean predator's yellowfin members can reach 75 km/h — what is it?
Tuna: Tribe of fish. Tuna (pl.: tunas or tuna) is a saltwater fish that belongs to the tribe Thunnini, a subgrouping of the Scombridae (mackerel) family.
Caused by white blood cells migrating into and damaging vessel walls, this group of disorders inflames both arteries and veins, and sometimes even the lymphatic vessels — what condition is it?
Vasculitis: Medical disorders that destroy blood vessels by inflammation.
With a heart-shaped white facial disc and an eerie screech instead of a hoot, this nocturnal hunter locates small mammals purely by sound — which bird?
Western barn owl: Species of owl. The western barn owl (Tyto alba) is a species of barn owl native to Europe, southwestern Asia, and Africa.

Known for quoting multiple religious scriptures in English lectures delivered in a suit and tie rather than traditional robes, this Indian preacher had his foundation banned in 2016 amid hate-speech and money-laundering accusations. Who is he?
